---
title: "About"
description: "What Economic Series Explorer shows, where the data comes from, and credits."
---

## Purpose

Economic Series Explorer puts market indices, output, prices, labour and interest-rate series on one date axis, so they can be compared over any window, up to their full history.

## How it works

- A pipeline in R fetches every series once a day (06:00 UTC) and commits the data to the repository as JSON. The site is static; all computation runs in the browser.
- **Indexed**: level series are set to 100 on the start date; rate series show the change from the start date in percentage points.
- **Actual values**: one series as stored, on a linear or log scale. Inflation is stored as the year-over-year change of the consumer price index, not the index itself.
- Windows longer than ten years draw daily series as weekly averages. Indexing and CSV export always use the full daily data.

## Sources

Market indices and the dollar index are adjusted closes from [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/). All other series come from [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/), Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sources = (await fetch("data/series.json")).json()
SOURCE_LABEL = ({ yahoo: "Yahoo Finance", fred: "FRED" })
html`<table class="table table-sm sources">
  <thead><tr><th>Series</th><th>Source</th><th>Symbol</th><th>Unit</th><th>From</th><th>To</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>${sources.map((s) => html`<tr>
    <td>${s.name}</td><td>${SOURCE_LABEL[s.source] ?? s.source}</td><td><code>${s.symbol}</code></td>
    <td>${s.unit}</td><td>${s.first_date}</td><td>${s.last_date}</td>
  </tr>`)}</tbody>
</table>`
```
